- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.77) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.27) — add 2–5% to forecast for low sentiment days.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent high sentiment — cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak.
- Forecast mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0) within 3–5 days, reduce forecast 3–7% to account for reversal risk.
- Overshoots after spikes are common — if forecast >15% above prior 30d high, apply downward correction of 5–10%.
- Forecast should not exceed 10% above or below 18d moving average unless sentiment strongly supports it.
